CLASS zcl_find_ceo DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS find_ceo_name
      RETURNING VALUE(rv_name) TYPE zemp_master-name.

ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_find_ceo IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD find_ceo_name.

    DATA: lt_employees   TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF zemp_master-employee_id WITH EMPTY KEY,
          lt_supervisors TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF zorg_structure-supervisor_id WITH EMPTY KEY,
          lv_ceo_id      TYPE zemp_master-employee_id,
          lv_count       TYPE i.

    " Get all employee IDs from the org structure (those who have a supervisor)
    SELECT employee_id FROM zorg_structure INTO TABLE @lt_employees.
    IF sy-subrc <> 0 OR lines( lt_employees ) = 0.
      " No org structure at all - cannot determine CEO
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    " Collect all unique person IDs involved in the org structure
    " (both as employees and as supervisors)
    DATA: lt_all_ids TYPE SORTED TABLE OF zemp_master-employee_id WITH UNIQUE KEY table_line.

    SELECT DISTINCT employee_id FROM zorg_structure INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_emp_ids).
    SELECT DISTINCT supervisor_id FROM zorg_structure INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_sup_ids).

    LOOP AT lt_emp_ids INTO DATA(ls_emp).
      INSERT ls_emp-employee_id INTO TABLE lt_all_ids.
    ENDLOOP.
    LOOP AT lt_sup_ids INTO DATA(ls_sup).
      INSERT ls_sup-supervisor_id INTO TABLE lt_all_ids.
    ENDLOOP.

    " The CEO is someone who appears in the set of all persons involved
    " but does NOT appear as an employee_id in zorg_structure
    " (i.e., they have no supervisor)
    DATA: lt_candidates TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF zemp_master-employee_id WITH EMPTY KEY.

    LOOP AT lt_all_ids INTO DATA(lv_id).
      READ TABLE lt_emp_ids WITH KEY employee_id = lv_id TRANSPORTING NO FIELDS.
      IF sy-subrc <> 0.
        " This person has no supervisor entry -> candidate for CEO
        APPEND lv_id TO lt_candidates.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

    " There must be exactly one CEO candidate
    IF lines( lt_candidates ) <> 1.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    lv_ceo_id = lt_candidates[ 1 ].

    " Verify the CEO exists in the employee master
    SELECT SINGLE name FROM zemp_master
      WHERE employee_id = @lv_ceo_id
      INTO @rv_name.

    IF sy-subrc <> 0.
      CLEAR rv_name.
    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

    " indirectly) but is never listed as an employee in zorg_structure.

    " Step 1: Get all distinct supervisor IDs from org structure
    " Step 2: Remove those who also appear as employee_id in org structure

    " The CEO does NOT appear as employee_id in zorg_structure.

    " zorg_structure-employee_id.

    SELECT e~employee_id
      FROM zemp_master AS e
      LEFT OUTER JOIN zorg_structure AS o

    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM zemp_master INTO @DATA(lv_emp_count).

      RETURN.

      RETURN.

  METHOD find_ceo_name.

    DATA lt_candidates TYPE TABLE OF char20.
    DATA lt_children TYPE TABLE OF char20.
    DATA lv_child TYPE char20.
    DATA lv_emp_count TYPE i.
    DATA lv_org_count TYPE i.
    DATA lv_invalid_supervisors TYPE i.
    DATA lt_visited TYPE SORTED TABLE OF char20 WITH UNIQUE KEY table_line.
    DATA lt_current TYPE TABLE OF char20.

    " CEO = employee in zemp_master whose employee_id is NOT in
    " zorg_structure-employee_id (everyone except CEO has a row as employee).
    SELECT e~employee_id
      FROM zemp_master AS e
      LEFT OUTER JOIN zorg_structure AS o
        ON e~employee_id = o~employee_id
      WHERE o~employee_id IS NULL
      INTO TABLE @lt_candidates.

    " There must be exactly one candidate for a clear CEO
    IF lines( lt_candidates ) <> 1.
      CLEAR rv_name.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    DATA(lv_ceo_id) = lt_candidates[ 1 ].

    " Count employees and org entries
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM zemp_master INTO @lv_emp_count.
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM zorg_structure INTO @lv_org_count.

    " If only one employee and no org structure, that's valid (single employee = CEO)
    IF lv_emp_count = 1 AND lv_org_count = 0.
      SELECT SINGLE name FROM zemp_master WHERE employee_id = @lv_ceo_id INTO @rv_name.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    " If there are multiple employees, org structure must have exactly emp_count - 1 entries
    IF lv_org_count <> lv_emp_count - 1.
      CLEAR rv_name.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    " Validate all supervisor_ids reference existing employees
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM zorg_structure AS o
      LEFT OUTER JOIN zemp_master AS e
        ON o~supervisor_id = e~employee_id
      WHERE e~employee_id IS NULL
      INTO @lv_invalid_supervisors.

    IF lv_invalid_supervisors > 0.
      CLEAR rv_name.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    " Verify the CEO is reachable as root: traverse from CEO downward and count
    " reachable employees. All employees must be reachable.
    APPEND lv_ceo_id TO lt_current.
    INSERT lv_ceo_id INTO TABLE lt_visited.

      SELECT employee_id FROM zorg_structure
        FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @lt_current
        WHERE supervisor_id = @lt_current-table_line
        INTO TABLE @lt_children.

        IF NOT line_exists( lt_visited[ table_line = lv_child ] ).

      CLEAR rv_name.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    DATA lt_candidates TYPE TABLE OF char20.

    " Find all employees who do not appear as employee_id in zorg_structure
    " (i.e., they have no supervisor). The CEO is the only such person.
    SELECT e~employee_id
      FROM zemp_master AS e
      WHERE NOT EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM zorg_structure AS o WHERE o~employee_id = e~employee_id )
      INTO TABLE @lt_candidates.

      " Single employee, no org structure needed - they are the CEO only if
      " there are no entries in zorg_structure
      SELECT COUNT(*) FROM zorg_structure INTO @lv_org_count.
      IF lv_org_count <> 0.
        RETURN.
      ENDIF.
    ELSE.
      " Multiple employees: verify the org structure count matches emp_count - 1
      SELECT COUNT(*) FROM zorg_structure INTO @lv_org_count.
      IF lv_org_count <> lv_emp_count - 1.
        RETURN.

      DATA lv_sup_count TYPE i.
      SELECT COUNT(*) FROM zorg_structure
        WHERE supervisor_id = @lv_ceo_id
        INTO @lv_sup_count.
      IF lv_sup_count = 0.
        RETURN.
      ENDIF.
    ENDIF.

    " Retrieve the CEO name
    SELECT SINGLE name FROM zemp_master
      WHERE employee_id = @lv_ceo_id
      INTO @rv_name.

  ENDMETHOD.

    """
    Given a positive integer n, you have to make a pile of n levels of stones.
    The first level has n stones.
    The number of stones in the next level is:
        - the next odd number if n is odd.
        - the next even number if n is even.
    Return the number of stones in each level in a list, where element at index
    i represents the number of stones in the level (i+1).

    Examples:
    >>> make_a_pile(3)
    [3, 5, 7]
    """

  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.

CLASS zcl_make_a_pile IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD make_a_pile.
    DATA(lv_stones) = iv_n.

    DO iv_n TIMES.
      APPEND lv_stones TO rt_result.
      lv_stones = lv_stones + 2.

def minPath(grid, k):
    """
    Given a grid with N rows and N columns (N >= 2) and a positive integer k, 
    each cell of the grid contains a value. Every integer in the range [1, N * N]
    inclusive appears exactly once on the cells of the grid.

    You have to find the minimum path of length k in the grid. You can start
    from any cell, and in each step you can move to any of the neighbor cells,
    in other words, you can go to cells which share an edge with you current
    cell.
    Please note that a path of length k means visiting exactly k cells (not
    necessarily distinct).
    You CANNOT go off the grid.
    A path A (of length k) is considered less than a path B (of length k) if
    after making the ordered lists of the values on the cells that A and B go
    through (let's call them lst_A and lst_B), lst_A is lexicographically less
    than lst_B, in other words, there exist an integer index i (1 <= i <= k)
    such that lst_A[i] < lst_B[i] and for any j (1 <= j < i) we have
    lst_A[j] = lst_B[j].
    It is guaranteed that the answer is unique.
    Return an ordered list of the values on the cells that the minimum path go through.

    Examples:

        Input: grid = [ [1,2,3], [4,5,6], [7,8,9]], k = 3
        Output: [1, 2, 1]

        Input: grid = [ [5,9,3], [4,1,6], [7,8,2]], k = 1
        Output: [1]
    """

CLASS zcl_min_path DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES:
      tt_int    TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF i WITH EMPTY KEY,
      tt_grid   TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF tt_int WITH EMPTY KEY.

    CLASS-METHODS min_path
      IMPORTING
        grid          TYPE tt_grid
        k             TYPE i
      RETURNING
        VALUE(result) TYPE tt_int.

  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_min_path IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD min_path.
    DATA: n          TYPE i,
          min_val    TYPE i,
          min_row    TYPE i,
          min_col    TYPE i,
          min_neigh  TYPE i,
          cell_val   TYPE i,
          cur_row    TYPE i,
          cur_col    TYPE i,
          neigh_val  TYPE i.

    n = lines( grid ).

    " Find the position of value 1 (the global minimum)
    min_val = n * n + 1.
    DO n TIMES.
      DATA(r) = sy-index.
      DATA(row_data) = grid[ r ].
      DO n TIMES.
        DATA(c) = sy-index.
        cell_val = row_data[ c ].
        IF cell_val < min_val.
          min_val = cell_val.
          min_row = r.
          min_col = c.
        ENDIF.
      ENDDO.
    ENDDO.

    " Find the minimum neighbor value of cell with value 1
    min_neigh = n * n + 1.
    " Up
    IF min_row > 1.
      DATA(up_row) = grid[ min_row - 1 ].
      neigh_val = up_row[ min_col ].
      IF neigh_val < min_neigh.
        min_neigh = neigh_val.
      ENDIF.
    ENDIF.
    " Down
    IF min_row < n.
      DATA(down_row) = grid[ min_row + 1 ].
      neigh_val = down_row[ min_col ].
      IF neigh_val < min_neigh.
        min_neigh = neigh_val.
      ENDIF.
    ENDIF.
    " Left
    IF min_col > 1.
      DATA(cur_row_data) = grid[ min_row ].
      neigh_val = cur_row_data[ min_col - 1 ].
      IF neigh_val < min_neigh.
        min_neigh = neigh_val.
      ENDIF.
    ENDIF.
    " Right
    IF min_col < n.
      cur_row_data = grid[ min_row ].
      neigh_val = cur_row_data[ min_col + 1 ].
      IF neigh_val < min_neigh.
        min_neigh = neigh_val.
      ENDIF.
    ENDIF.

    " Build the result path
    " The optimal path alternates between 1 and its minimum neighbor
    " For k steps: starts with 1, then min_neigh, then 1, ...
    DO k TIMES.
      DATA(idx) = sy-index.
      IF idx MOD 2 = 1.
        APPEND min_val TO result.
      ELSE.
        APPEND min_neigh TO result.
      ENDIF.
    ENDDO.

  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

def minPath(grid, k):
    """
    Given a grid with N rows and N columns (N >= 2) and a positive integer k, 
    each cell of the grid contains a value. Every integer in the range [1, N * N]
    inclusive appears exactly once on the cells of the grid.

    You have to find the minimum path of length k in the grid. You can start
    from any cell, and in each step you can move to any of the neighbor cells,
    in other words, you can go to cells which share an edge with you current
    cell.
    Please note that a path of length k means visiting exactly k cells (not
    necessarily distinct).
    You CANNOT go off the grid.
    A path A (of length k) is considered less than a path B (of length k) if
    after making the ordered lists of the values on the cells that A and B go
    through (let's call them lst_A and lst_B), lst_A is lexicographically less
    than lst_B, in other words, there exist an integer index i (1 <= i <= k)
    such that lst_A[i] < lst_B[i] and for any j (1 <= j < i) we have
    lst_A[j] = lst_B[j].
    It is guaranteed that the answer is unique.
    Return an ordered list of the values on the cells that the minimum path go through.

    Examples:

        Input: grid = [ [1,2,3], [4,5,6], [7,8,9]], k = 3
        Output: [1, 2, 1]

        Input: grid = [ [5,9,3], [4,1,6], [7,8,2]], k = 1

def minPath(grid, k):
    """
    Given a grid with N rows and N columns (N >= 2) and a positive integer k, 
    each cell of the grid contains a value. Every integer in the range [1, N * N]
    inclusive appears exactly once on the cells of the grid.

    You have to find the minimum path of length k in the grid. You can start
    from any cell, and in each step you can move to any of the neighbor cells,
    in other words, you can go to cells which share an edge with you current
    cell.
    Please note that a path of length k means visiting exactly k cells (not
    necessarily distinct).
    You CANNOT go off the grid.
    A path A (of length k) is considered less than a path B (of length k) if
    after making the ordered lists of the values on the cells that A and B go
    through (let's call them lst_A and lst_B), lst_A is lexicographically less
    than lst_B, in other words, there exist an integer index i (1 <= i <= k)
    such that lst_A[i] < lst_B[i] and for any j (1 <= j < i) we have
    lst_A[j] = lst_B[j].
    It is guaranteed that the answer is unique.
    Return an ordered list of the values on the cells that the minimum path go through.

    Examples:

        Input: grid = [ [1,2,3], [4,5,6], [7,8,9]], k = 3
        Output: [1, 2, 1]

        Input: grid = [ [5,9,3], [4,1,6], [7,8,2]], k = 1
        Output: [1]

          nc         TYPE i.

    n = lines( grid ).

    min_val = n * n + 1.
    min_row = 0.
    min_col = 0.

      DATA(row_data) = grid[ r ].

        DATA(c) = sy-index.

        IF val < min_val.

          min_row = r.
          min_col = c.

    APPEND 1 TO dr. APPEND 0 TO dc.

def minPath(grid, k):
    """
    Given a grid with N rows and N columns (N >= 2) and a positive integer k, 
    each cell of the grid contains a value. Every integer in the range [1, N * N]
    inclusive appears exactly once on the cells of the grid.

    You have to find the minimum path of length k in the grid. You can start
    from any cell, and in each step you can move to any of the neighbor cells,
    in other words, you can go to cells which share an edge with you current
    cell.
    Please note that a path of length k means visiting exactly k cells (not
    necessarily distinct).
    You CANNOT go off the grid.
    A path A (of length k) is considered less than a path B (of length k) if
    after making the ordered lists of the values on the cells that A and B go
    through (let's call them lst_A and lst_B), lst_A is lexicographically less
    than lst_B, in other words, there exist an integer index i (1 <= i <= k)
    such that lst_A[i] < lst_B[i] and for any j (1 <= j < i) we have
    lst_A[j] = lst_B[j].
    It is guaranteed that the answer is unique.
    Return an ordered list of the values on the cells that the minimum path go through.

    Examples:

        Input: grid = [ [1,2,3], [4,5,6], [7,8,9]], k = 3
        Output: [1, 2, 1]

        Input: grid = [ [5,9,3], [4,1,6], [7,8,2]], k = 1
        Output: [1]
    """

  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES:
      BEGIN OF ty_route_revenue,
        cityfrom      TYPE spfli-cityfrom,
        cityto        TYPE spfli-cityto,
        total_revenue TYPE p LENGTH 15 DECIMALS 2,
      END OF ty_route_revenue,
      ty_route_revenue_tab TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_route_revenue WITH EMPTY KEY.

      INNER JOIN sflight AS f ON f~carrid = s~carrid
                              AND f~connid = s~connid
      GROUP BY s~cityfrom, s~cityto
      ORDER BY total_revenue DESCENDING
      INTO CORRESPONDING FIELDS OF TABLE @rt_result.

  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

def rounded_avg(n, m):
    """You are given two positive integers n and m, and your task is to compute the
    average of the integers from n through m (including n and m). 
    Round the answer to the nearest integer and convert that to binary.
    If n is greater than m, return -1.
    Example:
    rounded_avg(1, 5) => "0b11"
    rounded_avg(7, 5) => -1
    rounded_avg(10, 20) => "0b1111"
    rounded_avg(20, 33) => "0b11010"
    """

CLASS zcl_rounded_avg DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS rounded_avg
      IMPORTING
        n             TYPE i
        m             TYPE i
      RETURNING
        VALUE(result) TYPE string.

  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS int_to_binary
      IMPORTING
        iv_number        TYPE i
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_binary) TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_rounded_avg IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD rounded_avg.
    IF n > m.
      result = '-1'.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    DATA(lv_sum) = 0.
    DATA(lv_count) = 0.
    DATA(lv_i) = n.
    WHILE lv_i <= m.
      lv_sum = lv_sum + lv_i.
      lv_count = lv_count + 1.
      lv_i = lv_i + 1.
    ENDWHILE.

    DATA(lv_avg) = round( val = CONV decfloat34( lv_sum ) / lv_count dec = 0 ).
    DATA(lv_avg_int) = CONV i( lv_avg ).

    result = |0b{ int_to_binary( lv_avg_int ) }|.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD int_to_binary.
    DATA(lv_number) = iv_number.

    IF lv_number = 0.
      rv_binary = '0'.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    rv_binary = ''.
    WHILE lv_number > 0.
      DATA(lv_remainder) = lv_number MOD 2.
      rv_binary = |{ lv_remainder }{ rv_binary }|.
      lv_number = lv_number DIV 2.
    ENDWHILE.
  ENDMETHOD.

def select_words(s, n):
    """Given a string s and a natural number n, you have been tasked to implement 
    a function that returns a list of all words from string s that contain exactly 
    n consonants, in order these words appear in the string s.
    If the string s is empty then the function should return an empty list.
    Note: you may assume the input string contains only letters and spaces.
    Examples:
    select_words("Mary had a little lamb", 4) ==> ["little"]
    select_words("Mary had a little lamb", 3) ==> ["Mary", "lamb"]
    select_words("simple white space", 2) ==> []
    select_words("Hello world", 4) ==> ["world"]
    select_words("Uncle sam", 3) ==> ["Uncle"]
    """

CLASS zcl_select_words DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS select_words
      IMPORTING
        iv_s            TYPE string
        iv_n            TYPE i
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_words) TYPE string_table.

  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS count_consonants
      IMPORTING
        iv_word        TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_count) TYPE i.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_select_words IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD select_words.
    DATA: lt_parts TYPE string_table,
          lv_word  TYPE string.

    CLEAR rt_words.

    IF iv_s IS INITIAL.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    SPLIT iv_s AT space INTO TABLE lt_parts.

    LOOP AT lt_parts INTO lv_word.
      IF lv_word IS NOT INITIAL.
        IF count_consonants( lv_word ) = iv_n.
          APPEND lv_word TO rt_words.
        ENDIF.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD count_consonants.
    DATA: lv_len    TYPE i,
          lv_index  TYPE i,
          lv_char   TYPE c LENGTH 1,
          lv_lower  TYPE string.

    rv_count = 0.
    lv_lower = to_lower( iv_word ).
    lv_len = strlen( lv_lower ).
    lv_index = 0.

    WHILE lv_index < lv_len.
      lv_char = lv_lower+lv_index(1).
      IF lv_char CA 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'.
        IF NOT ( lv_char CA 'aeiou' ).
          rv_count = rv_count + 1.
        ENDIF.
      ENDIF.
      lv_index = lv_index + 1.
    ENDWHILE.

  ENDMETHOD.

def sort_array(arr):
    """
    In this Kata, you have to sort an array of non-negative integers according to
    number of ones in their binary representation in ascending order.
    For similar number of ones, sort based on decimal value.

    It must be implemented like this:
    >>> sort_array([1, 5, 2, 3, 4]) == [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
    >>> sort_array([-2, -3, -4, -5, -6]) == [-6, -5, -4, -3, -2]
    >>> sort_array([1, 0, 2, 3, 4]) [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
    """

CLASS zcl_sort_array DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: tt_integers TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF i WITH EMPTY KEY.

    CLASS-METHODS sort_array
      IMPORTING
        it_arr           TYPE tt_integers
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_result) TYPE tt_integers.

  PRIVATE SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sort_entry,
             value    TYPE i,
             ones     TYPE i,
           END OF ty_sort_entry,
           tt_sort_entries TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_sort_entry WITH EMPTY KEY.

    CLASS-METHODS count_ones
      IMPORTING
        iv_value       TYPE i
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_ones) TYPE i.

ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_sort_array IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD sort_array.

    DATA: lt_entries TYPE tt_sort_entries,
          ls_entry   TYPE ty_sort_entry.

    LOOP AT it_arr INTO DATA(lv_val).
      ls_entry-value = lv_val.
      ls_entry-ones  = count_ones( lv_val ).
      APPEND ls_entry TO lt_entries.
    ENDLOOP.

    SORT lt_entries BY ones ASCENDING value ASCENDING.

    LOOP AT lt_entries INTO ls_entry.
      APPEND ls_entry-value TO rt_result.
    ENDLOOP.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD count_ones.

    DATA: lv_abs   TYPE i,
          lv_temp  TYPE i,
          lv_count TYPE i VALUE 0.

    IF iv_value >= 0.
      lv_abs = iv_value.
    ELSE.
      lv_abs = iv_value * -1.
    ENDIF.

    lv_temp = lv_abs.

    WHILE lv_temp > 0.
      IF lv_temp MOD 2 = 1.
        lv_count = lv_count + 1.
      ENDIF.
      lv_temp = lv_temp / 2.
    ENDWHILE.

    rv_ones = lv_count.

  ENDMETHOD.

from typing import List


def parse_music(music_string: str) -> List[int]:
    """ Input to this function is a string representing musical notes in a special ASCII format.
    Your task is to parse this string and return list of integers corresponding to how many beats does each
    not last.

    Here is a legend:
    'o' - whole note, lasts four beats
    'o|' - half note, lasts two beats
    '.|' - quater note, lasts one beat

    >>> parse_music('o o| .| o| o| .| .| .| .| o o')
    [4, 2, 1, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 4, 4]
    """

CLASS zcl_parse_music DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS parse_music
      IMPORTING
        iv_music_string TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_beats) TYPE int4_table.

  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_parse_music IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD parse_music.
    DATA: lt_tokens TYPE TABLE OF string,
          lv_beat   TYPE i.

    IF iv_music_string IS INITIAL.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    SPLIT iv_music_string AT space INTO TABLE lt_tokens.

    LOOP AT lt_tokens INTO DATA(lv_token).
      IF lv_token IS INITIAL.
        CONTINUE.
      ENDIF.

      CASE lv_token.
        WHEN 'o'.
          lv_beat = 4.
        WHEN 'o|'.
          lv_beat = 2.
        WHEN '.|'.
          lv_beat = 1.
        WHEN OTHERS.
          CONTINUE.
      ENDCASE.

      APPEND lv_beat TO rt_beats.
    ENDLOOP.

  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

def f(n):
    """ Implement the function f that takes n as a parameter,
    and returns a list of size n, such that the value of the element at index i is the factorial of i if i is even
    or the sum of numbers from 1 to i otherwise.
    i starts from 1.
    the factorial of i is the multiplication of the numbers from 1 to i (1 * 2 * ... * i).
    Example:
    f(5) == [1, 2, 6, 24, 15]
    """

CLASS zcl_function_f DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS execute
      IMPORTING
        iv_n          TYPE i
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_result) TYPE int4_table.

  PRIVATE SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS factorial
      IMPORTING
        iv_i          TYPE i
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_result) TYPE i.

    CLASS-METHODS sum_1_to_i
      IMPORTING
        iv_i          TYPE i
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_result) TYPE i.

ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_function_f IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD execute.
    DATA lv_value TYPE i.

    DO iv_n TIMES.
      DATA(lv_i) = sy-index.

      IF lv_i MOD 2 = 0.
        lv_value = factorial( lv_i ).
      ELSE.
        lv_value = sum_1_to_i( lv_i ).
      ENDIF.

      APPEND lv_value TO rt_result.
    ENDDO.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD factorial.
    rv_result = 1.
    DO iv_i TIMES.
      rv_result = rv_result * sy-index.
    ENDDO.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD sum_1_to_i.
    rv_result = iv_i * ( iv_i + 1 ) / 2.
  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_delivery_date_calculator DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS calculate_delivery_date
      IMPORTING
        order_date      TYPE string
        mat_id          TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(delivery_date) TYPE d.

  PRIVATE SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS is_working_day
      IMPORTING
        iv_date       TYPE d
        it_holidays   TYPE STANDARD TABLE
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_result) TYPE abap_bool.

ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_delivery_date_calculator IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD calculate_delivery_date.

    DATA: lv_lead_time TYPE i,
          lv_order_date TYPE d,
          lv_date       TYPE d,
          lt_holidays   TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF zholiday,
          ls_material   TYPE zmaterial,
          lv_mat_id     TYPE zmaterial-mat_id.

    " Convert order_date string to date
    " Expected format: YYYY-MM-DD
    DATA(lv_date_str) TYPE string.
    lv_date_str = order_date.
    REPLACE ALL OCCURRENCES OF '-' IN lv_date_str WITH ''.
    lv_order_date = lv_date_str.

    " Get lead time from zmaterial
    lv_mat_id = mat_id.
    SELECT SINGLE * FROM zmaterial INTO ls_material WHERE mat_id = lv_mat_id.
    IF sy-subrc = 0.
      lv_lead_time = ls_material-lead_time_days.
    ELSE.
      lv_lead_time = 0.
    ENDIF.

    " Get holidays
    SELECT * FROM zholiday INTO TABLE lt_holidays.

    " If lead time is 0, return order date
    IF lv_lead_time = 0.
      delivery_date = lv_order_date.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    " Calculate delivery date by adding working days
    lv_date = lv_order_date.
    DATA(lv_days_added) = 0.

    WHILE lv_days_added < lv_lead_time.
      lv_date = lv_date + 1.
      IF is_working_day( iv_date = lv_date it_holidays = lt_holidays ) = abap_true.
        lv_days_added = lv_days_added + 1.
      ENDIF.
    ENDWHILE.

    delivery_date = lv_date.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD is_working_day.

    DATA: lv_day_of_week TYPE i,
          ls_holiday     TYPE zholiday.

    " Check if weekend (Saturday = 6, Sunday = 7)
    " CALL FUNCTION to get day of week
    DATA: lv_date TYPE d.
    lv_date = iv_date.

    CALL FUNCTION 'DATE_COMPUTE_DAY'
      EXPORTING
        date = lv_date
      IMPORTING
        day  = lv_day_of_week.

    " 6 = Saturday, 7 = Sunday
    IF lv_day_of_week = 6 OR lv_day_of_week = 7.
      rv_result = abap_false.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    " Check if holiday
    LOOP AT it_holidays INTO ls_holiday.
      IF ls_holiday-holiday_date = lv_date.
        rv_result = abap_false.
        RETURN.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

    rv_result = abap_true.

  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_critical_path DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS calculate_min_total_duration
      RETURNING VALUE(rv_duration) TYPE i.

  PRIVATE SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_step,
             step_id  TYPE c LENGTH 10,
             duration TYPE i,
           END OF ty_step.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_dep,
             from_step TYPE c LENGTH 10,
             to_step   TYPE c LENGTH 10,
           END OF ty_dep.

    TYPES ty_steps TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_step WITH KEY step_id.
    TYPES ty_deps TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_dep WITH KEY from_step to_step.

    CLASS-METHODS get_longest_path
      IMPORTING
        it_steps           TYPE ty_steps
        it_deps            TYPE ty_deps
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_duration) TYPE i.

    CLASS-METHODS visit
      IMPORTING
        iv_step_id     TYPE c LENGTH 10
        it_steps       TYPE ty_steps
        it_deps        TYPE ty_deps
      CHANGING
        ct_earliest    TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_step WITH UNIQUE KEY step_id
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_time) TYPE i.

ENDCLASS.


CLASS zcl_critical_path IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD calculate_min_total_duration.

    DATA: lt_steps TYPE ty_steps,
          lt_deps  TYPE ty_deps.

    SELECT step_id, duration FROM zfs_data INTO TABLE @lt_steps.
    SELECT from_step, to_step FROM zfnet_data INTO TABLE @lt_deps.

    rv_duration = get_longest_path(
      it_steps = lt_steps
      it_deps  = lt_deps
    ).

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD get_longest_path.

    DATA: lt_earliest TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_step WITH UNIQUE KEY step_id.
    DATA: lv_time TYPE i.

    " For each step, compute the earliest completion time via DFS with memoization
    LOOP AT it_steps INTO DATA(ls_step).
      lv_time = visit(
        iv_step_id = ls_step-step_id
        it_steps   = it_steps
        it_deps    = it_deps
        CHANGING ct_earliest = lt_earliest
      ).
      IF lv_time > rv_duration.
        rv_duration = lv_time.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD visit.

    " Check if already computed (memoization)
    READ TABLE ct_earliest WITH KEY step_id = iv_step_id INTO DATA(ls_cached).
    IF sy-subrc = 0.
      rv_time = ls_cached-duration.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    " Get the duration of the current step
    DATA(lv_own_duration) = VALUE i( ).

  METHOD calculate_min_total_duration.

    DATA: lt_steps TYPE ty_steps,
          lt_deps  TYPE ty_deps.

    SELECT step_id, duration FROM zfs_data INTO TABLE @lt_steps.
    SELECT from_step, to_step FROM zfnet_data INTO TABLE @lt_deps.

    rv_duration = get_longest_path(
      it_steps = lt_steps
      it_deps  = lt_deps
    ).

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD get_longest_path.

    DATA: lt_earliest TYPE SORTED TABLE OF ty_step WITH UNIQUE KEY step_id.
    DATA: lv_max TYPE i VALUE 0.

    " For each step, compute the earliest finish time via DFS/memoization
    LOOP AT it_steps ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_step>).
      DATA(lv_finish) = visit(
        iv_step_id  = <fs_step>-step_id
        it_steps    = it_steps
        it_deps     = it_deps
        CHANGING ct_earliest = lt_earliest
      ).
      IF lv_finish > lv_max.
        lv_max = lv_finish.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

    rv_duration = lv_max.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD visit.

    " Check if already computed
    READ TABLE ct_earliest WITH KEY step_id = iv_step_id ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_cached>).
    IF sy-subrc = 0.
      rv_et = <fs_cached>-duration.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    " Get the duration of the current step
    DATA(lv_own_duration) = VALUE i( ).
    READ TABLE it_steps WITH KEY step_id = iv_step_id ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_step>).
    IF sy-subrc = 0.
      lv_own_duration = <fs_step>-duration.
    ENDIF.

    " Find the maximum earliest finish time among all predecessors
    DATA(lv_max_pred_finish) = 0.

    LOOP AT it_deps ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_dep>) WHERE to_step = iv_step_id.
      DATA(lv_pred_finish) = visit(
        iv_step_id  = <fs_dep>-from_step
        it_steps    = it_steps
        it_deps     = it_deps
        CHANGING ct_earliest = ct_earliest
      ).
      IF lv_pred_finish > lv_max_pred_finish.
        lv_max_pred_finish = lv_pred_finish.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

def is_palindrome(string: str) -> bool:
    """ Test if given string is a palindrome """
    return string == string[::-1]


def make_palindrome(string: str) -> str:
    """ Find the shortest palindrome that begins with a supplied string.
    Algorithm idea is simple:
    - Find the longest postfix of supplied string that is a palindrome.
    - Append to the end of the string reverse of a string prefix that comes before the palindromic suffix.
    >>> make_palindrome('')
    ''
    >>> make_palindrome('cat')
    'catac'
    >>> make_palindrome('cata')
    'catac'
    """

CLASS zcl_make_palindrome DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS make_palindrome
      IMPORTING
        iv_string        TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_result) TYPE string.

  PRIVATE SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS is_palindrome
      IMPORTING
        iv_string        TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_result) TYPE abap_bool.

ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_make_palindrome IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD is_palindrome.
    DATA(lv_len) = strlen( iv_string ).
    DATA(lv_reversed) = VALUE string( ).
    DATA(lv_index) = lv_len - 1.

    WHILE lv_index >= 0.
      lv_reversed = lv_reversed && iv_string+lv_index(1).
      lv_index = lv_index - 1.
    ENDWHILE.

    IF iv_string = lv_reversed.
      rv_result = abap_true.
    ELSE.
      rv_result = abap_false.
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD make_palindrome.
    IF iv_string IS INITIAL.
      rv_result = ||.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    DATA(lv_len) = strlen( iv_string ).

    " Find the longest postfix that is a palindrome
    DATA(lv_i) = 0.
    WHILE lv_i < lv_len.
      DATA(lv_suffix) = substring( val = iv_string off = lv_i len = lv_len - lv_i ).
      IF is_palindrome( lv_suffix ) = abap_true.
        EXIT.
      ENDIF.
      lv_i = lv_i + 1.
    ENDWHILE.

    " Get the prefix before the palindromic suffix
    DATA(lv_prefix) = substring( val = iv_string off = 0 len = lv_i ).

    " Reverse the prefix
    DATA(lv_prefix_len) = strlen( lv_prefix ).
    DATA(lv_reversed_prefix) = VALUE string( ).
    DATA(lv_index) = lv_prefix_len - 1.

    WHILE lv_index >= 0.
      lv_reversed_prefix = lv_reversed_prefix && lv_prefix+lv_index(1).
      lv_index = lv_index - 1.
    ENDWHILE.

    " Append reversed prefix to the end of the original string
    rv_result = iv_string && lv_reversed_prefix.
  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_histogram DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES:
      BEGIN OF ty_entry,
        letter TYPE string,
        count  TYPE i,
      END OF ty_entry,
      ty_entries TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_entry WITH DEFAULT KEY.

    CLASS-METHODS histogram
      IMPORTING
        iv_test          TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_result) TYPE ty_entries.

  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_histogram IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD histogram.
    DATA: lt_words   TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF string,
          lv_word    TYPE string,
          lv_max     TYPE i,
          lv_found   TYPE abap_bool,
          ls_entry   TYPE ty_entry.

    CLEAR rt_result.

    IF iv_test IS INITIAL.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    SPLIT iv_test AT space INTO TABLE lt_words.

    DATA lt_counts TYPE ty_entries.

    LOOP AT lt_words INTO lv_word.
      IF lv_word IS INITIAL.
        CONTINUE.
      ENDIF.

      lv_found = abap_false.
      LOOP AT lt_counts ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_count>) WHERE letter = lv_word.
        <fs_count>-count = <fs_count>-count + 1.
        lv_found = abap_true.
        EXIT.
      ENDLOOP.

      IF lv_found = abap_false.
        ls_entry-letter = lv_word.
        ls_entry-count  = 1.
        APPEND ls_entry TO lt_counts.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

    " Find the maximum count
    lv_max = 0.
    LOOP AT lt_counts INTO ls_entry.
      IF ls_entry-count > lv_max.
        lv_max = ls_entry-count.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

    " Return all entries with the maximum count
    LOOP AT lt_counts INTO ls_entry WHERE count = lv_max.
      APPEND ls_entry TO rt_result.
    ENDLOOP.

  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

def by_length(arr):
    """
    Given an array of integers, sort the integers that are between 1 and 9 inclusive,
    reverse the resulting array, and then replace each digit by its corresponding name from
    "One", "Two", "Three", "Four", "Five", "Six", "Seven", "Eight", "Nine".

    For example:
      arr = [2, 1, 1, 4, 5, 8, 2, 3]   
            -> sort arr -> [1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8] 
            -> reverse arr -> [8, 5, 4, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1]
      return ["Eight", "Five", "Four", "Three", "Two", "Two", "One", "One"]
    
      If the array is empty, return an empty array:
      arr = []
      return []
    
      If the array has any strange number ignore it:
      arr = [1, -1 , 55] 
            -> sort arr -> [-1, 1, 55]
            -> reverse arr -> [55, 1, -1]
      return = ['One']
    """

CLASS zcl_by_length DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES:
      tt_int    TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF i WITH EMPTY KEY,
      tt_string TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF string WITH EMPTY KEY.

    CLASS-METHODS by_length
      IMPORTING
        it_arr           TYPE tt_int
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_result) TYPE tt_string.

  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_by_length IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD by_length.

    DATA: lt_filtered TYPE tt_int.

    " Filter only integers between 1 and 9 inclusive
    LOOP AT it_arr INTO DATA(lv_val).
      IF lv_val >= 1 AND lv_val <= 9.
        APPEND lv_val TO lt_filtered.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

    " Sort ascending
    SORT lt_filtered BY table_line ASCENDING.

    " Reverse the sorted array
    DATA(lv_lines) = lines( lt_filtered ).
    DATA: lt_reversed TYPE tt_int.
    DO lv_lines TIMES.
      DATA(lv_index) = lv_lines - sy-index + 1.
      APPEND lt_filtered[ lv_index ] TO lt_reversed.
    ENDDO.

    " Map each digit to its name
    DATA: lt_names TYPE tt_string.
    APPEND 'One'   TO lt_names.
    APPEND 'Two'   TO lt_names.
    APPEND 'Three' TO lt_names.
    APPEND 'Four'  TO lt_names.
    APPEND 'Five'  TO lt_names.
    APPEND 'Six'   TO lt_names.
    APPEND 'Seven' TO lt_names.
    APPEND 'Eight' TO lt_names.
    APPEND 'Nine'  TO lt_names.

    LOOP AT lt_reversed INTO lv_val.
      APPEND lt_names[ lv_val ] TO rt_result.
    ENDLOOP.

  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

def exchange(lst1, lst2):
    """In this problem, you will implement a function that takes two lists of numbers,
    and determines whether it is possible to perform an exchange of elements
    between them to make lst1 a list of only even numbers.
    There is no limit on the number of exchanged elements between lst1 and lst2.
    If it is possible to exchange elements between the lst1 and lst2 to make
    all the elements of lst1 to be even, return "YES".
    Otherwise, return "NO".
    For example:
    exchange([1, 2, 3, 4], [1, 2, 3, 4]) => "YES"
    exchange([1, 2, 3, 4], [1, 5, 3, 4]) => "NO"
    It is assumed that the input lists will be non-empty.
    """

CLASS zcl_exchange DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_num,
             num TYPE i,
           END OF ty_num,
           tt_num TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_num WITH EMPTY KEY.

    CLASS-METHODS exchange
      IMPORTING
        it_lst1         TYPE tt_num
        it_lst2         TYPE tt_num
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_result) TYPE string.

  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_exchange IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD exchange.
    DATA: lv_odd_count_lst1  TYPE i,
          lv_even_count_lst2 TYPE i.

    " Count odd numbers in lst1
    LOOP AT it_lst1 INTO DATA(ls_num1).
      IF ls_num1-num MOD 2 <> 0.
        lv_odd_count_lst1 = lv_odd_count_lst1 + 1.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

    " Count even numbers in lst2
    LOOP AT it_lst2 INTO DATA(ls_num2).
      IF ls_num2-num MOD 2 = 0.
        lv_even_count_lst2 = lv_even_count_lst2 + 1.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

    " If there are enough even numbers in lst2 to replace all odd numbers in lst1
    IF lv_even_count_lst2 >= lv_odd_count_lst1.
      rv_result = |YES|.
    ELSE.
      rv_result = |NO|.
    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

def prime_fib(n: int):
    """
    prime_fib returns n-th number that is a Fibonacci number and it's also prime.
    >>> prime_fib(1)
    2
    >>> prime_fib(2)
    3
    >>> prime_fib(3)
    5
    >>> prime_fib(4)
    13
    >>> prime_fib(5)
    89
    """

CLASS zcl_prime_fib DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS prime_fib
      IMPORTING
        n             TYPE i
      RETURNING
        VALUE(result) TYPE int8.

  PRIVATE SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS is_prime
      IMPORTING
        num           TYPE int8
      RETURNING
        VALUE(result) TYPE abap_bool.

ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_prime_fib IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD prime_fib.
    DATA: fib_prev TYPE int8 VALUE 0,
          fib_curr TYPE int8 VALUE 1,
          fib_next TYPE int8,
          count    TYPE i VALUE 0.

    WHILE count < n.
      fib_next = fib_prev + fib_curr.
      fib_prev = fib_curr.
      fib_curr = fib_next.

      IF is_prime( fib_curr ) = abap_true.
        count = count + 1.
        IF count = n.
          result = fib_curr.
          RETURN.
        ENDIF.
      ENDIF.
    ENDWHILE.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD is_prime.
    IF num < 2.
      result = abap_false.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    IF num = 2 OR num = 3.
      result = abap_true.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    IF num MOD 2 = 0 OR num MOD 3 = 0.
      result = abap_false.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    DATA(i) = CONV int8( 5 ).
    WHILE i * i <= num.
      IF num MOD i = 0 OR num MOD ( i + 2 ) = 0.
        result = abap_false.
        RETURN.
      ENDIF.
      i = i + 6.
    ENDWHILE.

    result = abap_true.
  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

Implement an abap class with a static method that checks if the employee hierarchy is valid. 
The method should:
- Read all entries from ZORG_STRUCTURE.
- Return abap_true if the organizational structure satisfies all of the following:
   - Each employee has at most one direct manager.
   - There are no cycles in the manager relationships.
   - There is exactly one top-level manager (a "CEO") without a manager.
   - All employees are directly or indirectly connected to the CEO.
- Return abap_false otherwise.
Use this table: 
define table zorg_structure {
    key employee_id   : abap.char(20) not null;
    key supervisor_id : abap.char(20) not null;
}

Example:
Input:
DATA(zorg_entries) = VALUE zorg_structure ( 
  ( employee_id = 'A' superior_id = 'B' )
  ( employee_id = 'B' superior_id = 'C' )
  ( employee_id = 'C' superior_id = 'D' )
)
INSERT zorg_structure FROM TABLE @zorg_structure.
Output:
DATA(result) = zcl_hierarchy_utils=>is_valid_hierarchy( ).
" result = abap_true.

CLASS zcl_hierarchy_utils DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS is_valid_hierarchy
      RETURNING VALUE(rv_valid) TYPE abap_bool.

  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_hierarchy_utils IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD is_valid_hierarchy.

    DATA: lt_org TYPE TABLE OF zorg_structure,
          lt_employees TYPE SORTED TABLE OF zorg_structure-employee_id WITH UNIQUE KEY table_line,
          lt_all_people TYPE SORTED TABLE OF zorg_structure-employee_id WITH UNIQUE KEY table_line,
          lt_supervisors TYPE SORTED TABLE OF zorg_structure-supervisor_id WITH UNIQUE KEY table_line,
          lt_ceos TYPE TABLE OF zorg_structure-employee_id,
          lv_current TYPE zorg_structure-employee_id,
          lv_steps TYPE i,
          lv_total_people TYPE i,
          lt_reachable TYPE SORTED TABLE OF zorg_structure-employee_id WITH UNIQUE KEY table_line,
          lt_queue TYPE TABLE OF zorg_structure-employee_id,
          lv_person TYPE zorg_structure-employee_id,
          lv_cycle TYPE abap_bool.

    rv_valid = abap_false.

    SELECT * FROM zorg_structure INTO TABLE @lt_org.

    " If no entries, no employees, no CEO => invalid (need exactly one CEO)
    IF lt_org IS INITIAL.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    " Check: each employee has at most one direct manager
    " Since employee_id + supervisor_id is the key, an employee could appear
    " multiple times with different supervisors
    DATA lt_emp_count TYPE TABLE OF zorg_structure-employee_id.
    LOOP AT lt_org INTO DATA(ls_org).
      APPEND ls_org-employee_id TO lt_emp_count.
    ENDLOOP.
    SORT lt_emp_count.
    DATA lv_prev TYPE zorg_structure-employee_id VALUE ''.
    DATA lv_count TYPE i VALUE 0.
    LOOP AT lt_emp_count INTO DATA(lv_emp).
      IF lv_emp <> lv_prev.
        IF lv_count > 1.
          RETURN.
        ENDIF.
        lv_prev = lv_emp.
        lv_count = 1.
      ELSE.
        lv_count = lv_count + 1.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.
    IF lv_count > 1.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    " Collect all unique employees (those who appear as employee_id)
    LOOP AT lt_org INTO ls_org.
      INSERT ls_org-employee_id INTO TABLE lt_employees.
    ENDLOOP.

    " Collect all unique people (employees + supervisors)
    LOOP AT lt_org INTO ls_org.
      INSERT ls_org-employee_id INTO TABLE lt_all_people.
      INSERT ls_org-supervisor_id INTO TABLE lt_all_people.
    ENDLOOP.

    " Find CEOs: people who appear as supervisor but never as employee,
    " plus anyone in all_people who is not in employees
    LOOP AT lt_all_people INTO lv_person.
      READ TABLE lt_employees WITH KEY table_line = lv_person TRANSPORTING NO FIELDS.
      IF sy-subrc <> 0.
        APPEND lv_person TO lt_ceos.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

    " There must be exactly one CEO
    IF lines( lt_ceos ) <> 1.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    DATA(lv_ceo) = lt_ceos[ 1 ].

    " Check for cycles: for each employee, follow the supervisor chain.
    " If we visit more nodes than total people, there's a cycle.
    lv_total_people = lines( lt_all_people ).

    LOOP AT lt_employees INTO lv_emp.
      lv_current = lv_emp.
      lv_steps = 0.
      lv_cycle = abap_false.
      WHILE lv_steps <= lv_total_people.
        READ TABLE lt_org WITH KEY employee_id = lv_current INTO DATA(ls_found).
        IF sy-subrc <> 0.
          " Reached someone with no manager
          EXIT.
        ENDIF.
        lv_current = ls_found-supervisor_id.
        lv_steps = lv_steps + 1.
        IF lv_steps > lv_total_people.
          lv_cycle = abap_true.
        ENDIF.
      ENDWHILE.
      IF lv_cycle = abap_true.
        RETURN.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

    " Check all employees are connected to the CEO:
    " BFS/DFS from CEO downwards using supervisor relationships
    APPEND lv_ceo TO lt_queue.
    INSERT lv_ceo INTO TABLE lt_reachable.

    WHILE lt_queue IS NOT INITIAL.
      lv_person = lt_queue[ 1 ].
      DELETE lt_queue INDEX 1.

      LOOP AT lt_org INTO ls_org WHERE supervisor_id = lv_person.
        INSERT ls_org-employee_id INTO TABLE lt_reachable.
        IF sy-subrc = 0.
          APPEND ls_org-employee_id TO lt_queue.
        ENDIF.
      ENDLOOP.
    ENDWHILE.

    " All people must be reachable
    IF lines( lt_reachable ) <> lines( lt_all_people ).
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    rv_valid = abap_true.

  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

  METHOD is_valid_hierarchy.

    DATA: lt_org TYPE TABLE OF zorg_structure,
          lt_employees TYPE SORTED TABLE OF string WITH NON-UNIQUE KEY table_line,
          lt_all_nodes TYPE SORTED TABLE OF string WITH UNIQUE KEY table_line,
          lt_managers TYPE TABLE OF string,
          lt_visited TYPE SORTED TABLE OF string WITH UNIQUE KEY table_line,
          lt_queue TYPE TABLE OF string,
          lv_employee TYPE string,
          lv_supervisor TYPE string,
          lv_ceo TYPE string,
          lv_count TYPE i,
          lv_current TYPE string.

    rv_valid = abap_false.

    SELECT * FROM zorg_structure INTO TABLE @lt_org.

    " If table is empty, no employees means no valid hierarchy
    IF lt_org IS INITIAL.
      rv_valid = abap_false.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    " Check: each employee has at most one direct manager
    " Since employee_id and supervisor_id are both key fields,
    " an employee could appear multiple times with different supervisors.
    " We need to check that each employee_id has at most one supervisor_id.
    DATA lt_emp_check TYPE TABLE OF string.
    LOOP AT lt_org ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<ls_org>).
      lv_employee = <ls_org>-employee_id.
      lv_supervisor = <ls_org>-supervisor_id.

      " Count how many managers this employee has
      DATA(lv_mgr_count) = 0.
      LOOP AT lt_org ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<ls_check>)
        WHERE employee_id = <ls_org>-employee_id.
        lv_mgr_count = lv_mgr_count + 1.
      ENDLOOP.
      IF lv_mgr_count > 1.
        RETURN.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

    " Collect all unique nodes (both employees and supervisors)
    LOOP AT lt_org ASSIGNING <ls_org>.
      lv_employee = <ls_org>-employee_id.
      lv_supervisor = <ls_org>-supervisor_id.
      INSERT lv_employee INTO TABLE lt_all_nodes.
      INSERT lv_supervisor INTO TABLE lt_all_nodes.
    ENDLOOP.

    " Find top-level managers: nodes that appear as supervisor but never as employee
    DATA lt_employees_with_mgr TYPE SORTED TABLE OF string WITH UNIQUE KEY table_line.
    LOOP AT lt_org ASSIGNING <ls_org>.
      lv_employee = <ls_org>-employee_id.
      INSERT lv_employee INTO TABLE lt_employees_with_mgr.
    ENDLOOP.

    DATA lt_ceos TYPE TABLE OF string.
    LOOP AT lt_all_nodes INTO DATA(lv_node).
      READ TABLE lt_employees_with_mgr WITH KEY table_line = lv_node TRANSPORTING NO FIELDS.
      IF sy-subrc <> 0.
        APPEND lv_node TO lt_ceos.

    IF lines( lt_ceos ) <> 1.
      RETURN.

    READ TABLE lt_ceos INDEX 1 INTO lv_ceo.

    " Check for cycles and connectivity using BFS from CEO downward
    APPEND lv_ceo TO lt_queue.
    INSERT lv_ceo INTO TABLE lt_visited.

    WHILE lt_queue IS NOT INITIAL.

      DELETE lt_queue INDEX 1.

      LOOP AT lt_org ASSIGNING <ls_org>

        lv_employee = <ls_org>-employee_id.

          " Already visited - cycle detected
          RETURN.
        ENDIF.

        INSERT lv_employee INTO TABLE lt_visited.
        APPEND lv_employee TO lt_queue.
      ENDLOOP.

    " Check all nodes are reachable from CEO
    IF lines( lt_visited ) <> lines( lt_all_nodes ).

CLASS zcl_hierarchy_utils IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD is_valid_hierarchy.

    DATA: lt_org TYPE TABLE OF zorg_structure,
          lt_employees TYPE SORTED TABLE OF zorg_structure-employee_id WITH UNIQUE KEY table_line,
          lt_all_people TYPE SORTED TABLE OF zorg_structure-employee_id WITH UNIQUE KEY table_line,
          lt_supervisors TYPE SORTED TABLE OF zorg_structure-supervisor_id WITH UNIQUE KEY KEY table_line COMPONENTS table_line,
          lt_ceos TYPE TABLE OF zorg_structure-employee_id,
          lv_ceo TYPE zorg_structure-employee_id,
          lt_reachable TYPE SORTED TABLE OF zorg_structure-employee_id WITH UNIQUE KEY table_line,
          lt_queue TYPE TABLE OF zorg_structure-employee_id,
          lv_current TYPE zorg_structure-employee_id,
          lv_index TYPE i.

    rv_valid = abap_false.

    SELECT * FROM zorg_structure INTO TABLE @lt_org.

    " If table is empty, no employees means no CEO => invalid
    IF lt_org IS INITIAL.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    " Check: each employee has at most one direct manager
    " Since employee_id + supervisor_id is the key, an employee could appear
    " multiple times with different supervisors. Check for duplicate employee_ids.
    DATA lt_emp_check TYPE TABLE OF zorg_structure-employee_id.
    LOOP AT lt_org INTO DATA(ls_org).
      APPEND ls_org-employee_id TO lt_emp_check.
    ENDLOOP.
    SORT lt_emp_check.
    DATA lv_prev TYPE zorg_structure-employee_id VALUE ''.
    DATA lv_first TYPE abap_bool VALUE abap_true.
    LOOP AT lt_emp_check INTO DATA(lv_emp).
      IF lv_first = abap_false AND lv_emp = lv_prev.
        " Duplicate employee => more than one manager
        RETURN.
      ENDIF.
      lv_prev = lv_emp.
      lv_first = abap_false.
    ENDLOOP.

    " Collect all unique employee IDs (those who appear as employee_id)
    LOOP AT lt_org INTO ls_org.
      INSERT ls_org-employee_id INTO TABLE lt_employees.
    ENDLOOP.

    " Collect all unique people (employees + supervisors)
    lt_all_people = lt_employees.
    LOOP AT lt_org INTO ls_org.
      INSERT ls_org-supervisor_id INTO TABLE lt_all_people.
    ENDLOOP.

    " Collect all supervisor IDs
    LOOP AT lt_org INTO ls_org.
      INSERT ls_org-supervisor_id INTO TABLE lt_supervisors.
    ENDLOOP.

    " Find CEOs: people who appear in all_people but NOT as an employee_id
    " (i.e., they have no manager assigned to them)
    LOOP AT lt_all_people INTO DATA(lv_person).
      READ TABLE lt_employees WITH KEY table_line = lv_person TRANSPORTING NO FIELDS.
      IF sy-subrc <> 0.
        APPEND lv_person TO lt_ceos.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

    " There must be exactly one CEO
    IF lines( lt_ceos ) <> 1.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    lv_ceo = lt_ceos[ 1 ].

    " Check for cycles: traverse from CEO downward; all people must be reachable
    " BFS from CEO through subordinates
    APPEND lv_ceo TO lt_queue.
    INSERT lv_ceo INTO TABLE lt_reachable.

    lv_index = 1.
    WHILE lv_index <= lines( lt_queue ).
      lv_current = lt_queue[ lv_index ].
      lv_index = lv_index + 1.

      " Find all direct reports of lv_current
      LOOP AT lt_org INTO ls_org WHERE supervisor_id = lv_current.
        READ TABLE lt_reachable WITH KEY table_line = ls_org-employee_id TRANSPORTING NO FIELDS.
        IF sy-subrc <> 0.
          INSERT ls_org-employee_id INTO TABLE lt_reachable.
          APPEND ls_org-employee_id TO lt_queue.
        ENDIF.
      ENDLOOP.
    ENDWHILE.

    " All people must be reachable from CEO
    IF lines( lt_reachable ) <> lines( lt_all_people ).
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    " If we reached here, all conditions are satisfied
    rv_valid = abap_true.

  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

    DATA: lt_org TYPE TABLE OF zorg_structure,

      RETURN.

    " Check: each employee has at most one direct manager

    " multiple times with different supervisors
    DATA lt_emp_count TYPE TABLE OF zorg_structure-employee_id.

        RETURN.
      ENDIF.
      INSERT ls_org-employee_id INTO TABLE lt_emp_sup.
    ENDLOOP.

    " Collect all people (employees and supervisors)
    LOOP AT lt_org INTO ls_org.
      INSERT ls_org-employee_id INTO TABLE lt_all_people.
      INSERT ls_org-supervisor_id INTO TABLE lt_all_people.
      INSERT ls_org-employee_id INTO TABLE lt_employees.
      INSERT ls_org-supervisor_id INTO TABLE lt_supervisors.

    " but NOT as employees (i.e., they have no manager)

      ENDLOOP.
    ENDWHILE.

def derivative(xs: list):
    """ xs represent coefficients of a polynomial.
    xs[0] + xs[1] * x + xs[2] * x^2 + ....
     Return derivative of this polynomial in the same form.
    >>> derivative([3, 1, 2, 4, 5])
    [1, 4, 12, 20]
    >>> derivative([1, 2, 3])
    [2, 6]
    """

CLASS zcl_polynomial_derivative DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: tt_coefficients TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF decfloat34 WITH EMPTY KEY.

    CLASS-METHODS derivative
      IMPORTING
        it_xs            TYPE tt_coefficients
      RETURNING

  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_polynomial_derivative IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD derivative.
    DATA: lv_index TYPE i VALUE 0.

    LOOP AT it_xs INTO DATA(lv_coeff).
      IF lv_index > 0.
        APPEND ( lv_coeff * lv_index ) TO rt_result.
      ENDIF.
      lv_index = lv_index + 1.
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

    returns a string encrypted with the alphabet being rotated. 
    The alphabet should be rotated in a manner such that the letters 
    shift down by two multiplied to two places.
    For example:
    encrypt('hi') returns 'lm'
    encrypt('asdfghjkl') returns 'ewhjklnop'
    encrypt('gf') returns 'kj'
    encrypt('et') returns 'ix'
    """

CLASS zcl_encrypt DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS encrypt
      IMPORTING
        iv_input         TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_result) TYPE string.

  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_encrypt IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD encrypt.
    DATA: lv_len    TYPE i,
          lv_index  TYPE i,
          lv_char   TYPE c LENGTH 1,
          lv_offset TYPE i,
          lv_new    TYPE i.

    CONSTANTS: lc_lower TYPE string VALUE 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz',
               lc_upper TYPE string VALUE 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ'.

    lv_len = strlen( iv_input ).

    DO lv_len TIMES.
      lv_index = sy-index - 1.

        FIND lv_char IN lc_upper MATCH OFFSET lv_offset.
        IF sy-subrc = 0.
          lv_new = ( lv_offset + 4 ) MOD 26.
          rv_result = rv_result && lc_upper+lv_new(1).
        ELSE.
          rv_result = rv_result && lv_char.
        ENDIF.
      ENDIF.
    ENDDO.

  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

    """
    Given two positive integers a and b, return the even digits between a
    and b, in ascending order.

    For example:
    generate_integers(2, 8) => [2, 4, 6, 8]
    generate_integers(8, 2) => [2, 4, 6, 8]

def sort_array(array):
    """
    Given an array of non-negative integers, return a copy of the given array after sorting,
    you will sort the given array in ascending order if the sum( first index value, last index value) is odd,
    or sort it in descending order if the sum( first index value, last index value) is even.

    Note:
    * don't change the given array.

    Examples:
    * sort_array([]) => []
    * sort_array([5]) => [5]
    * sort_array([2, 4, 3, 0, 1, 5]) => [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
    * sort_array([2, 4, 3, 0, 1, 5, 6]) => [6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0]
    """

CLASS zcl_sort_array DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: tt_integers TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF i WITH EMPTY KEY.

    CLASS-METHODS sort_array
      IMPORTING
        it_array        TYPE tt_integers
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_result) TYPE tt_integers.

  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_sort_array IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD sort_array.
    DATA(lv_lines) = lines( it_array ).

    IF lv_lines <= 1.
      rt_result = it_array.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    rt_result = it_array.

    DATA(lv_first) = it_array[ 1 ].
    DATA(lv_last)  = it_array[ lv_lines ].
    DATA(lv_sum)   = lv_first + lv_last.

    IF lv_sum MOD 2 = 1.
      " Odd sum: ascending order
      SORT rt_result BY table_line ASCENDING.
    ELSE.
      " Even sum: descending order
      SORT rt_result BY table_line DESCENDING.
    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

    Addition ( + )

        MODIFY lt_operands INDEX lv_idx FROM lv_left.

    are not correct planet names.

    bf("Earth", "Mercury") ==> ("Venus")
    bf("Mercury", "Uranus") ==> ("Venus", "Earth", "Mars", "Jupiter", "Saturn")

CLASS zcl_bf_planets DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PROTECTED SECTION.

  METHOD bf.
    DATA(lv_index1) = get_planet_index( iv_planet1 ).
    DATA(lv_index2) = get_planet_index( iv_planet2 ).

    IF lv_index1 = 0 OR lv_index2 = 0.

    DATA(lt_planets) = VALUE ty_planet_table(

      ( |Venus| )
      ( |Earth| )
      ( |Mars| )
      ( |Jupiter| )
      ( |Saturn| )
      ( |Uranus| )
      ( |Neptune| )
    ).

    DATA(lv_idx) = 0.
    LOOP AT lt_planets INTO DATA(lv_planet).
      lv_idx = lv_idx + 1.
      IF lv_idx > lv_lower AND lv_idx < lv_upper.

      WHEN 'Jupiter'  THEN 5
      WHEN 'Saturn'   THEN 6
      WHEN 'Uranus'   THEN 7
      WHEN 'Neptune'  THEN 8
      ELSE 0
    ).

    '''
    Write a function that accepts two lists of strings and returns the list that has 
    total number of chars in the all strings of the list less than the other list.

    if the two lists have the same number of chars, return the first list.

    Examples
    total_match([], []) ➞ []
    total_match(['hi', 'admin'], ['hI', 'Hi']) ➞ ['hI', 'Hi']
    total_match(['hi', 'admin'], ['hi', 'hi', 'admin', 'project']) ➞ ['hi', 'admin']

    of unique characters. If multiple strings have maximum number of unique
    characters, return the one which comes first in lexicographical order.

    find_max(["name", "of", "string"]) == "string"
    find_max(["name", "enam", "game"]) == "enam"
    find_max(["aaaaaaa", "bb" ,"cc"]) == ""aaaaaaa"

      IMPORTING

      RETURNING
        VALUE(count) TYPE i.

  METHOD find_max.
    DATA: max_unique TYPE i VALUE 0,
          curr_unique TYPE i.

    LOOP AT words INTO DATA(word).
      curr_unique = count_unique_chars( word ).
      IF curr_unique > max_unique.
        max_unique = curr_unique.
        result = word.
      ELSEIF curr_unique = max_unique.
        IF word < result.

        ENDIF.

    DO len TIMES.

      READ TABLE chars WITH KEY table_line = char TRANSPORTING NO FIELDS.
      IF sy-subrc <> 0.
        APPEND char TO chars.
      ENDIF.
    ENDDO.

    count = lines( chars ).
  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

    '''
    Given the lengths of the three sides of a triangle. Return the area of
    the triangle rounded to 2 decimal points if the three sides form a valid triangle. 
    Otherwise return -1
    Three sides make a valid triangle when the sum of any two sides is greater 
    than the third side.
    Example:
    triangle_area(3, 4, 5) == 6.00
    triangle_area(1, 2, 10) == -1
    '''

  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.

      IMPORTING
        iv_a          TYPE decfloat34

  PRIVATE SECTION.

  METHOD calculate_area.

    IF iv_a + iv_b > iv_c AND iv_a + iv_c > iv_b AND iv_b + iv_c > iv_a.

      rv_area = round( val = lv_area dec = 2 mode = cl_abap_math=>round_half_up ).

    and return the result as a string.
    If shift > number of digits, return digits reversed.

CLASS zcl_circular_shift DEFINITION

def smallest_change(arr):
    """
    Given an array arr of integers, find the minimum number of elements that
    need to be changed to make the array palindromic. A palindromic array is an array that
    is read the same backwards and forwards. In one change, you can change one element to any other element.

    For example:
    smallest_change([1,2,3,5,4,7,9,6]) == 4
    smallest_change([1, 2, 3, 4, 3, 2, 2]) == 1
    smallest_change([1, 2, 3, 2, 1]) == 0
    """

CLASS zcl_smallest_change DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS smallest_change
      IMPORTING
        arr           TYPE STANDARD TABLE
      RETURNING
        VALUE(result) TYPE i.

  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_smallest_change IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD smallest_change.
    DATA: lv_left  TYPE i,
          lv_right TYPE i,
          lv_count TYPE i,
          lv_len   TYPE i,
          lv_val_left  TYPE i,
          lv_val_right TYPE i.

    lv_len = lines( arr ).
    lv_left = 1.
    lv_right = lv_len.
    lv_count = 0.

    WHILE lv_left < lv_right.
      ASSIGN arr[ lv_left ] TO FIELD-SYMBOL(<left>).
      ASSIGN arr[ lv_right ] TO FIELD-SYMBOL(<right>).

      lv_val_left = <left>.
      lv_val_right = <right>.

      IF lv_val_left <> lv_val_right.
        lv_count = lv_count + 1.
      ENDIF.

      lv_left = lv_left + 1.
      lv_right = lv_right - 1.
    ENDWHILE.

    result = lv_count.
  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

    [1, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4]
    """

def closest_integer(value):
    '''
    Create a function that takes a value (string) representing a number
    and returns the closest integer to it. If the number is equidistant
    from two integers, round it away from zero.

    Examples
    >>> closest_integer("10")
    10
    >>> closest_integer("15.3")
    15

    Note:
    Rounding away from zero means that if the given number is equidistant
    from two integers, the one you should return is the one that is the
    farthest from zero. For example closest_integer("14.5") should
    return 15 and closest_integer("-14.5") should return -15.
    '''

CLASS zcl_closest_integer DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS closest_integer
      IMPORTING
        value         TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(result) TYPE i.

  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_closest_integer IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD closest_integer.

    DATA: lv_decimal  TYPE decfloat34,
          lv_fraction TYPE decfloat34,
          lv_abs_frac TYPE decfloat34,
          lv_truncated TYPE i.

    lv_decimal = value.

    lv_truncated = trunc( lv_decimal ).
    lv_fraction = lv_decimal - lv_truncated.
    lv_abs_frac = abs( lv_fraction ).

    IF lv_abs_frac < '0.5'.
      result = lv_truncated.
    ELSEIF lv_abs_frac > '0.5'.
      IF lv_decimal >= 0.
        result = lv_truncated + 1.
      ELSE.
        result = lv_truncated - 1.
      ENDIF.
    ELSE.
      " Equidistant case: round away from zero
      IF lv_decimal >= 0.
        result = lv_truncated + 1.
      ELSE.
        result = lv_truncated - 1.
      ENDIF.
    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

    '''
    Write a function that returns True if the object q will fly, and False otherwise.
    The object q will fly if it's balanced (it is a palindromic list) and the sum of its elements is less than or equal the maximum possible weight w.

    Example:
    will_it_fly([1, 2], 5) ➞ False 
    # 1+2 is less than the maximum possible weight, but it's unbalanced.

    will_it_fly([3, 2, 3], 1) ➞ False
    # it's balanced, but 3+2+3 is more than the maximum possible weight.

    will_it_fly([3, 2, 3], 9) ➞ True
    # 3+2+3 is less than the maximum possible weight, and it's balanced.

    will_it_fly([3], 5) ➞ True
    # 3 is less than the maximum possible weight, and it's balanced.
    '''

  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: tt_integers TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF i WITH EMPTY KEY.

    CLASS-METHODS will_it_fly
      IMPORTING
        q             TYPE tt_integers
        w             TYPE i
      RETURNING
        VALUE(result) TYPE abap_bool.

  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS is_palindrome
      IMPORTING
        q             TYPE tt_integers
      RETURNING
        VALUE(result) TYPE abap_bool.

  METHOD will_it_fly.
    DATA(lv_sum) = 0.
    LOOP AT q INTO DATA(lv_val).
      lv_sum = lv_sum + lv_val.
    ENDLOOP.

    IF is_palindrome( q ) = abap_true AND lv_sum <= w.
      result = abap_true.
    ELSE.
      result = abap_false.
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD is_palindrome.
    DATA(lv_lines) = lines( q ).
    result = abap_true.

    DATA(lv_index) = 1.
    WHILE lv_index <= lv_lines / 2.
      DATA(lv_left) = q[ lv_index ].
      DATA(lv_right) = q[ lv_lines - lv_index + 1 ].
      IF lv_left <> lv_right.

      lv_index = lv_index + 1.

def monotonic(l: list):
    """Return True is list elements are monotonically increasing or decreasing.
    >>> monotonic([1, 2, 4, 20])
    True
    >>> monotonic([1, 20, 4, 10])
    False
    >>> monotonic([4, 1, 0, -10])
    True
    """

CLASS zcl_monotonic DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS check_monotonic
      IMPORTING
        it_list          TYPE STANDARD TABLE
      RETURNING

  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.

CLASS zcl_monotonic IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD check_monotonic.

    DATA: lv_increasing TYPE abap_bool VALUE abap_true,
          lv_decreasing TYPE abap_bool VALUE abap_true,
          lv_current    TYPE i,
          lv_previous   TYPE i,
          lv_count      TYPE i,
          lv_index      TYPE i.

    lv_count = lines( it_list ).

    IF lv_count <= 1.
      rv_result = abap_true.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    lv_index = 0.

    LOOP AT it_list ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<ls_entry>).
      lv_index = lv_index + 1.
      lv_current = <ls_entry>.

      IF lv_index > 1.
        IF lv_current < lv_previous.
          lv_increasing = abap_false.
        ENDIF.
        IF lv_current > lv_previous.
          lv_decreasing = abap_false.
        ENDIF.
      ENDIF.

      lv_previous = lv_current.
    ENDLOOP.

    IF lv_increasing = abap_true OR lv_decreasing = abap_true.
      rv_result = abap_true.
    ELSE.
      rv_result = abap_false.
    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

    >>> int_to_mini_roman(19) == 'xix'

    DATA: lv_number TYPE i,
          lv_roman  TYPE string.

             value  TYPE i,
             symbol TYPE string,
           END OF ty_roman_map.

    DATA: lt_roman_map TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_roman_map WITH EMPTY KEY.

    lt_roman_map = VALUE #(
      ( value = 1000 symbol = `m` )
      ( value = 900  symbol = `cm` )
      ( value = 500  symbol = `d` )
      ( value = 400  symbol = `cd` )
      ( value = 100  symbol = `c` )
      ( value = 90   symbol = `xc` )
      ( value = 50   symbol = `l` )
      ( value = 40   symbol = `xl` )
      ( value = 10   symbol = `x` )
      ( value = 9    symbol = `ix` )
      ( value = 5    symbol = `v` )
      ( value = 4    symbol = `iv` )
      ( value = 1    symbol = `i` )
    ).

    lv_number = iv_number.
    lv_roman = ``.

    LOOP AT lt_roman_map INTO DATA(ls_map).
      WHILE lv_number >= ls_map-value.
        lv_roman = lv_roman && ls_map-symbol.
        lv_number = lv_number - ls_map-value.

def skjkasdkd(lst):
    """You are given a list of integers.
    You need to find the largest prime value and return the sum of its digits.

    Examples:
    For lst = [0,3,2,1,3,5,7,4,5,5,5,2,181,32,4,32,3,2,32,324,4,3] the output should be 10
    For lst = [1,0,1,8,2,4597,2,1,3,40,1,2,1,2,4,2,5,1] the output should be 25
    For lst = [1,3,1,32,5107,34,83278,109,163,23,2323,32,30,1,9,3] the output should be 13
    For lst = [0,724,32,71,99,32,6,0,5,91,83,0,5,6] the output should be 11
    For lst = [0,81,12,3,1,21] the output should be 3
    For lst = [0,8,1,2,1,7] the output should be 7
    """

CLASS zcl_largest_prime_digit_sum DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS find_largest_prime_digit_sum
      IMPORTING
        it_list       TYPE STANDARD TABLE
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_sum) TYPE i.

  PRIVATE SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS is_prime
      IMPORTING
        iv_number       TYPE i
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_prime) TYPE abap_bool.

CLASS zcl_largest_prime_digit_sum IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD find_largest_prime_digit_sum.

    DATA: lv_number       TYPE i,
          lv_largest_prime TYPE i,
          lv_found        TYPE abap_bool,
          lv_temp         TYPE i,
          lv_digit        TYPE i,
          lv_str          TYPE string.

    lv_largest_prime = -1.
    lv_found = abap_false.

    LOOP AT it_list INTO lv_number.
      IF lv_number > lv_largest_prime AND is_prime( lv_number ) = abap_true.
        lv_largest_prime = lv_number.
        lv_found = abap_true.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

    IF lv_found = abap_false.
      rv_sum = 0.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    lv_str = |{ lv_largest_prime }|.
    CONDENSE lv_str NO-GAPS.

    rv_sum = 0.
    DO strlen( lv_str ) TIMES.
      DATA(lv_index) TYPE i = sy-index - 1.
      DATA(lv_char) TYPE c LENGTH 1 = lv_str+lv_index(1).

    to students. The teacher has been making her own algorithm for grading.
    The only problem is, she has lost the code she used for grading.
    She has given you a list of GPAs for some students and you have to write 
    a function that can output a list of letter grades using the following table:
             GPA       |    Letter grade
              4.0                A+
            > 3.7                A 
            > 3.3                A- 
            > 3.0                B+
            > 2.7                B 
            > 2.3                B-
            > 2.0                C+
            > 1.7                C
            > 1.3                C-
            > 1.0                D+ 
            > 0.7                D 
            > 0.0                D-
              0.0                E
    

    Example:
    grade_equation([4.0, 3, 1.7, 2, 3.5]) ==> ['A+', 'B', 'C-', 'C', 'A-']
    """

CLASS zcl_numerical_letter_grade DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: ty_grades TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF decfloat34 WITH EMPTY KEY,

def words_in_sentence(sentence):
    """
    You are given a string representing a sentence,
    the sentence contains some words separated by a space,
    and you have to return a string that contains the words from the original sentence,
    whose lengths are prime numbers,
    the order of the words in the new string should be the same as the original one.

    Example 1:
        Input: sentence = "This is a test"
        Output: "is"

    Example 2:
        Input: sentence = "lets go for swimming"
        Output: "go for"

    Constraints:
        * 1 <= len(sentence) <= 100
        * sentence contains only letters
    """

CLASS zcl_words_in_sentence DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS words_in_sentence
      IMPORTING
        iv_sentence      TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_result) TYPE string.

  PRIVATE SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS is_prime
      IMPORTING
        iv_number       TYPE i
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_prime) TYPE abap_bool.

ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_words_in_sentence IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD words_in_sentence.
    DATA: lt_words  TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF string,
          lv_word   TYPE string,
          lv_len    TYPE i,
          lt_result TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF string.

    SPLIT iv_sentence AT space INTO TABLE lt_words.

    LOOP AT lt_words INTO lv_word.
      lv_len = strlen( lv_word ).
      IF is_prime( lv_len ) = abap_true.
        APPEND lv_word TO lt_result.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

    CONCATENATE LINES OF lt_result INTO rv_result SEPARATED BY space.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD is_prime.
    rv_prime = abap_false.

    IF iv_number < 2.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    IF iv_number = 2.
      rv_prime = abap_true.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    IF iv_number MOD 2 = 0.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    DATA(lv_i) = 3.
    WHILE lv_i * lv_i <= iv_number.
      IF iv_number MOD lv_i = 0.
        RETURN.
      ENDIF.
      lv_i = lv_i + 2.
    ENDWHILE.

    rv_prime = abap_true.
  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

def pluck(arr):
    """
    "Given an array representing a branch of a tree that has non-negative integer nodes
    your task is to pluck one of the nodes and return it.
    The plucked node should be the node with the smallest even value.
    If multiple nodes with the same smallest even value are found return the node that has smallest index.

    The plucked node should be returned in a list, [ smalest_value, its index ],
    If there are no even values or the given array is empty, return [].

    Example 1:
        Input: [4,2,3]
        Output: [2, 1]
        Explanation: 2 has the smallest even value, and 2 has the smallest index.

    Example 2:
        Input: [1,2,3]
        Output: [2, 1]
        Explanation: 2 has the smallest even value, and 2 has the smallest index. 

    Example 3:
        Input: []
        Output: []
    
    Example 4:
        Input: [5, 0, 3, 0, 4, 2]
        Output: [0, 1]
        Explanation: 0 is the smallest value, but  there are two zeros,
                     so we will choose the first zero, which has the smallest index.

    Constraints:
        * 1 <= nodes.length <= 10000
        * 0 <= node.value
    """

CLASS zcl_pluck DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES:
      tt_int TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF i WITH EMPTY KEY.

    CLASS-METHODS pluck
      IMPORTING
        arr           TYPE tt_int
      RETURNING
        VALUE(result) TYPE tt_int.

  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_pluck IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD pluck.
    DATA: lv_smallest_even  TYPE i VALUE -1,
          lv_smallest_index TYPE i VALUE -1.

    LOOP AT arr INTO DATA(lv_value).
      DATA(lv_index) = sy-tabix - 1.
      IF lv_value MOD 2 = 0.
        IF lv_smallest_even = -1 OR lv_value < lv_smallest_even.
          lv_smallest_even = lv_value.
          lv_smallest_index = lv_index.
        ENDIF.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

    IF lv_smallest_even >= 0.
      APPEND lv_smallest_even TO result.
      APPEND lv_smallest_index TO result.
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.

from typing import List


def parse_nested_parens(paren_string: str) -> List[int]:
    """ Input to this function is a string represented multiple groups for nested parentheses separated by spaces.
    For each of the group, output the deepest level of nesting of parentheses.
    E.g. (()()) has maximum two levels of nesting while ((())) has three.

    >>> parse_nested_parens('(()()) ((())) () ((())()())')
    [2, 3, 1, 3]
    """

CLASS zcl_parse_nested_parens DEFINITION
  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS parse_nested_parens
      IMPORTING
        iv_paren_string TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_result) TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF i WITH EMPTY KEY.

  PROTECTED SECTION.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS get_max_depth
      IMPORTING
        iv_group        TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_depth) TYPE i.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_parse_nested_parens IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD parse_nested_parens.
    DATA: lv_paren_string TYPE string,
          lt_groups       TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF string.

    lv_paren_string = iv_paren_string.
    CONDENSE lv_paren_string.

    SPLIT lv_paren_string AT space INTO TABLE lt_groups.

    LOOP AT lt_groups INTO DATA(lv_group).
      IF lv_group IS NOT INITIAL.
        APPEND get_max_depth( lv_group ) TO rt_result.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD get_max_depth.
    DATA: lv_current_depth TYPE i VALUE 0,
          lv_max_depth     TYPE i VALUE 0,
          lv_length        TYPE i,
          lv_index         TYPE i,

def file_name_check(file_name):
    """Create a function which takes a string representing a file's name, and returns
    'Yes' if the the file's name is valid, and returns 'No' otherwise.
    A file's name is considered to be valid if and only if all the following conditions 
    are met:
    - There should not be more than three digits ('0'-'9') in the file's name.
    - The file's name contains exactly one dot '.'
    - The substring before the dot should not be empty, and it starts with a letter from 
    the latin alphapet ('a'-'z' and 'A'-'Z').
    - The substring after the dot should be one of these: ['txt', 'exe', 'dll']
    Examples:
    file_name_check("example.txt") # => 'Yes'
    file_name_check("1example.dll") # => 'No' (the name should start with a latin alphapet letter)
    """

  PUBLIC
  FINAL
  CREATE PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS file_name_check
      IMPORTING

  PRIVATE SECTION.
ENDCLASS.

    DATA: lv_dot_count   TYPE i VALUE 0,
          lv_digit_count TYPE i VALUE 0,
          lv_len         TYPE i,
          lv_char        TYPE c LENGTH 1,
          lv_dot_pos     TYPE i VALUE -1,
          lv_before_dot  TYPE string,
          lv_after_dot   TYPE string,
          lv_first_char  TYPE c LENGTH 1.

    lv_len = strlen( iv_file_name ).

    " Count dots and digits
    DO lv_len TIMES.
      lv_char = iv_file_name+( sy-index - 1 )(1).
      IF lv_char = '.'.
        lv_dot_count = lv_dot_count + 1.
        lv_dot_pos = sy-index - 1.
      ENDIF.
      IF lv_char >= '0' AND lv_char <= '9'.
        lv_digit_count = lv_digit_count + 1.
      ENDIF.
    ENDDO.

    " Check exactly one dot
    IF lv_dot_count <> 1.
      rv_result = 'No'.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    " Check not more than three digits
    IF lv_digit_count > 3.
      rv_result = 'No'.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    " Split into before and after dot
    lv_before_dot = iv_file_name(lv_dot_pos).
    DATA(lv_after_start) = lv_dot_pos + 1.
    IF lv_after_start < lv_len.
      lv_after_dot = iv_file_name+lv_after_start.
    ELSE.
      lv_after_dot = ''.
    ENDIF.

    " Check substring before dot is not empty
    IF strlen( lv_before_dot ) = 0.
      rv_result = 'No'.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    " Check first character is a latin letter
    lv_first_char = lv_before_dot(1).
    IF NOT ( ( lv_first_char >= 'a' AND lv_first_char <= 'z' ) OR
             ( lv_first_char >= 'A' AND lv_first_char <= 'Z' ) ).
      rv_result = 'No'.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    " Check extension
    IF lv_after_dot <> 'txt' AND lv_after_dot <> 'exe' AND lv_after_dot <> 'dll'.
      rv_result = 'No'.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    rv_result = 'Yes'.
